# Use ai-adoption-rollout

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Plan the human rollout of an AI tool or workflow to an organisation — sized cohorts, enablement per cohort, named champions, a comms plan that states what will not change, and an adoption gate every wave must pass before the next one opens.

**Reach for it when** a tool has been chosen and the question is how it reaches people without stalling or backlash. Do NOT use to phase a technical cutover (that's migration-plan) or to choose which use case to roll out (that's ai-use-case-triage).

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install ai-adoption-rollout                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install ai-adoption-rollout --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install ai-adoption-rollout --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the AI engineering pack: [`--pack ai-engineering`](../packs/use-the-ai-engineering-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Plan how we roll this AI tool out to the org"
- "How do we drive adoption without a backlash?"
- "Design the cohorts and enablement for our AI launch"
- "Our last AI rollout decayed after launch — plan the retry"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Plan the phased migration of our database schema"
- "Which use case should we roll out first?"
- "Write the rules for what people can put into these tools"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use ai-adoption-rollout".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Cohorts get smaller-to-larger with a stated reason each**, and the plan refuses a single big-bang wave.
- **Every wave has an adoption gate with an observable, a threshold, and a bake time** — plus a rollback if it fails.
- **The outcome is a behaviour, not a usage number.** Licences activated is not adoption.
- **The comms plan states explicitly what will not change** (headcount, evaluation, how work is judged). Omitting it is a defect, not a tone choice.
- **Champions are roles with protected hours**, never names, and never unbudgeted.
- **Enablement is per cohort and hands-on with the participant's own work** — a single deck for everyone is the failure mode.
- **The friction loop names an owner and a cadence.**

## Use something else when

- Phasing a *technical* cutover (schema, API version, datastore) — that's `migration-plan`, which sequences systems, not people.
- Choosing which use case to roll out — that's [`ai-use-case-triage`](../../../packs/ai-engineering/skills/ai-use-case-triage/SKILL.md).
- Deciding whether the organisation is ready at all — that's [`ai-readiness-assessment`](../../../packs/ai-engineering/skills/ai-readiness-assessment/SKILL.md).
- Writing the rules for what may be put into the tool — that's [`ai-usage-policy`](../../../packs/ai-engineering/skills/ai-usage-policy/SKILL.md).
- Reporting on adoption that already happened — that's `ai-usage-report`.
